what: The Lean proof of Cui, Liu and Woodruff (lockqueue/intmul at 4738aeff: integer multiplication in O(n (log n)^(1 − 2^-46)) steps on a multi-stack Turing machine) against the statement file of the same release, SubNLogN/Challenge.lean. The statement is the release's own: this checks that the headline theorem proves exactly that proposition, on the three standard axioms, under a second kernel, and that the check refuses statements we changed. Whether the proposition is the paper's theorem is a reading, kept apart.

canonical.what: the release's own statement file: one fixed multi-stack machine with finite alphabets multiplies two binary naturals within (C·L)·(log2 L)^(1 − 2^-46) steps on every input of length L ≥ N₀, stated in ℕ

claim.what: the headline theorem of the release
claim.license: Apache-2.0 (the software of the repository); no byte of the file is kept here but its declaration's header

f3.what: the statement is an existence claim with no hypotheses to satisfy

f2NotApplicable: the statement quantifies over Turing machines and has no decidable instance to evaluate; the encodings it names are evaluated on small pairs by a separate check of the same audit
notInScope: the mathematics beyond what the kernel checks; whether a multi-stack machine's time is a multitape machine's time (a classical simulation, formalized by neither proof); the constants C and N₀, which the statement only asserts to exist
